about.tagline: Software engineer, tinkerer, and builder of things that work for a long time.

beyond.title: Husband & father
beyond.text: First and foremost, I'm a husband to the best, most beautiful, smart, and funny wife I could have met, and a father to a wonderful, spunky, and frightfully intelligent boy. When he's awake, I try to spend as much time as I can with him: watching him grow, feeding him strawberries, and playing piano together.

beyond.title: Gaming
beyond.text: I've always been a gamer. It's how I unwind, and honestly, it's part of what got me into software in the first place. Long RPG session or something competitive, I'm always down.

beyond.title: Anime
beyond.text: Yeah, I watch anime. My top 10 changes every season, though One Piece is almost always number one. If you want to talk about what's airing or debate subs vs. dubs, I'm your guy.

beyond.title: Home lab
beyond.text: I run my own home lab and love experimenting with infrastructure, self-hosting, and networking, and generally seeing how things work under the hood. If it has a config file, I'm going to mess with it.

projects.name: Marbles
projects.text: A digital version of a board game invented by my mom's side of the family. It brings out the best (and worst) in everyone at family gatherings, and I'd wanted to put it on a screen for years. It's finally live and playable.

cfg.label: Complete
cfg.headline: Software Engineer & Technology Leader
cfg.summary: I use software to innovate, automate, and improve development and user experiences. My skills lie heavily in scalable, full-stack web and native applications.
cfg.intro: I'm a software engineer in West Des Moines, Iowa, with a career spent building, breaking, fixing, and shipping software across a wild range of tech stacks. These days I wear two hats: Software Consultant at Source Allies, and the entire IT department at Patient Preferred.

basics.name: Ryan Jensen
basics.label: Software Engineer & Technology Leader
basics.summary: I use software to innovate, automate, and improve development and user experiences. My skills lie heavily in scalable, full-stack web and native applications.

work.name: Source Allies
work.summary: Consultant across 4+ client engagements in financial services, insurance, identity management, and enterprise web, spanning full-stack development, delivery leadership, coaching, and generative AI.
highlights: Ranked #1 interviewer for 2025 and the first half of 2026, with 30+ interviews and ~10 hires still with the company.
Technical delivery lead for a regional mutual insurer's data engineering engagement (SQL Server, T-SQL, Databricks, dbt), including project management and coaching.
Led English/French internationalization of a roofing-materials manufacturer's customer portal and outgoing email for the US and Canada (Vue I18n, Thymeleaf, Spring Boot).
Bootstrapped a generative AI initiative on AWS Bedrock.

Redesigning a federally backed bank's high-traffic web application, which handles all of its money intake: reworked the frontend, built its first public API and secured it, and moved identity to PingOne, migrating Active Directory and LDAP users.
Helped design a digital-identity company's webinar platform in Figma.
Mentor and teach the company's apprentices.

work.name: Patient Preferred Financial Services
work.note: Currently part-time, supporting new feature requests and regular software updates.
work.summary: Took over a clinic payment and patient-management platform from a larger development team and run it solo, reporting to leadership. Own technology strategy, budget, vendor relationships (DataX, ACHeck, Web.com), and security and compliance.
highlights: Cut monthly AWS costs ~91% (~$1,400 → ~$120) over three years while improving availability, stability, and speed.

Modernized the platform from an AngularJS frontend, .NET Framework API, and SQL Server with SQL Jobs on Windows Server 2012 EC2 instances to SSR Next.js on AWS via OpenNext, modern .NET Minimal APIs on AWS Lambda, PostgreSQL on AWS RDS, and crontab on a nano Linux instance.
Built resiliency and fallback plans into critical third-party integrations, including ACH payments.

work.name: Principal Financial Group
work.summary: Modernized legacy .NET applications and the pipelines that ship them.
highlights: Cut build times in existing pipelines by 80%+, tightening developer feedback loops.
Set up CI/CD in GitHub Actions and supported on-prem-to-AWS migrations using Lambda and SNS.

work.name: Wellabe, Inc.
work.summary: Led small teams modernizing the company's software and unifying its tech stack.
highlights: Led the team that owned the company's main revenue-generating product, training and supporting every engineer on it.
Mentored 7 junior and mid-level engineers and paired with each intern for their entire internship.
Migrated WPF desktop apps to Blazor web apps and improved the performance of legacy software.
Reengineered CI/CD to increase developer throughput and added test-coverage requirements.
Improved business-critical daily batch programs and built a department wiki to centralize documentation.

work.name: Far Reach Inc.
work.summary: Built full-stack features for a homegrown ERP system with Angular, RxJS, .NET, and SQL Server on Azure, using ASP.NET Boilerplate, PrimeNG, and Bootstrap, and upgraded the company's internal .NET applications.

work.name: Hy-Vee, Inc.
work.summary: Worked across legacy .NET and WinForms applications and greenfield React, Kotlin, Spring Boot, Ktor, and GraphQL services, federated with Apollo on Google Cloud.
highlights: Helped build a Tax API on a task force, managing product tax values for 450+ grocery and convenience stores and publishing updates to every store over pub/sub.
Seeded new stores with millions of tax records in batches, with a check after each batch that every item was accounted for.
Led the move of widely used shared libraries from a file share to GitHub, with CI/CD, artifact storage, and automated tests.
Cut CI/CD build times by 50%+.

work.name: Stine Seed, Inc.
work.summary: Built features for employee portals that manage seed production, packaging, and sales (Angular, .NET Core), set up CI/CD in Azure DevOps, and kept a tight feedback loop with users.

work.name: Brownells, Inc.
work.summary: Integrated a new third-party ERP with existing WMS and POS systems, building pub/sub message pathways and failover on IBM MQ, with a Razor Pages, jQuery, and Bootstrap frontend on .NET Framework APIs.

work.name: UPS
work.position: Package Handler → Local Sort Supervisor → Package Center Supervisor
work.summary: Promoted twice in two years. Supervised 30+ drivers and 40+ inside employees on safety, production, and attendance, and personally trained more than half of them.

highlights: Ran daytime delivery operations for every driver: kept routes on track, handled emergencies, and tracked fuel use, time-card accuracy, and the delivery-area map.
Ran the evening sort of 30+ package cars into five outbound trailers, and handled training, certifications, terminations, and personnel management.
Loaded and unloaded trucks, then processed international shipments for air and freight; trained in hazardous-materials handling and classification.

cfg.label: Engineering Manager
cfg.headline: Software Engineering Manager
cfg.summary: Engineering leader with 8+ years of full-stack software experience and nearly four years supervising frontline teams before that. I hire, mentor, and grow engineers, own technology strategy and budgets, and lead delivery across .NET, JVM, and JavaScript stacks on AWS and Azure.
cfg.intro: I've spent my career building, breaking, fixing, and shipping software, and these days a lot of that work is about people. I've been Source Allies' #1 interviewer, mentored apprentices and interns, and run a company's entire technology operation on my own. Before any of that, I ran sort crews and delivery routes at UPS, so leading a team isn't new to me.

cfg.summary: Full-stack engineer with 8+ years designing, modernizing, and shipping scalable systems across .NET, JVM, and JavaScript stacks. I lead technical delivery, architect cloud and serverless platforms, speed up CI/CD, and mentor the engineers around me.
cfg.intro: I love the craft. I've spent 8+ years building, breaking, fixing, and shipping software across .NET, JVM, and JavaScript stacks, and I'm happiest untangling the hard problem, modernizing the legacy system nobody wants to touch, and bringing the rest of the team along with me.
